newsitem.title: BELGIUM: IRISH-DUTCH PLAN FOR BELGIAN AIRPORTS - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: IRISH-DUTCH PLAN FOR BELGIAN AIRPORTS - PAPER.

text.p: A 50/50 joint venture set up by Dutch airport Luchthaven Schiphol NV and Ireland's Aer Rianta has presented Belgium's government with a plan to cooperate with Belgian airports, Belgian newspaper De Financieel Economische Tijd reported on Friday.

Under the plan, Schiphol and Brussels airport would cooperate on international flights, while Gosselies airport in Charleroi, Belgium, would take over private charter and budget airline services. Belgium's Ostend and Bierset airports could also be used to handle some freight and courier services diverted from the other airports, the newspaper said.

It was not immediately clear how the plan would work in practice, but the proposal comes as the Belgian government is considering merging the Brussels airport company with the country's civil aviation authority into a new limited liability company, possibly ahead of privatisation.

This could open the way for the consortium to take a stake or manage the new Belgian airports company, De Tijd said. The consortium's proposal had been welcomed in government quarters, but negotiations had not started.

The Dutch government is also presently considering the privatisation of Schiphol, which is linked to discussions about whether to build a new international airport elsewhere in the country. A decision is due to be taken at the end of 1997.
De Tijd said Schiphol sees the consortium's proposal as a solution to its own capacity problems.
